ca3ca1.summary: Most mechanisms in the CA3->CA1/skip/comparator/temporal-loop track are re-descriptions of published work. CA3 retrieval is modern-Hopfield attention (Ramsauer 2020; Whittington 2021); the successor store is Sompolinsky & Kanter 1986/Chaudhry 2023; the CA1 fusion vector is the InferSent/heuristic-matching feature; CA1-as-prediction-error is Chen et al. 2024 (Neuron); the closed loop of lagged self-states is the Feedback Transformer; the time channel is the Laplace layer of Shankar & Howard (and DeepSITH), with relatives in RetNet decays and CoPE. Genuinely new or unusual: explicit loop-gain analysis of a memory re-injection channel with a confirmed critical gain (K_c=1.680, period 44.1 tokens, reproduced), the delayed rho-periodic rectified re-entry kernel, and sparse-write/dense-read addressing. Main problems: (1) the docs deny a CA1->CA3 pyramidal back-projection that tracing has found (Lin 2021/2023); (2) the 'high-pass' account of subtractive feedback ignores Bode's integral: at K=1 DC echo halves but ~46-token content is amplified 2.5x; (3) the CA1 comparator is mistimed (successor prediction vs current input), and novelty is distilled token loss, not comparator output; (4) the block lacks the EC-II->CA3 path and puts CA2 in series; (5) the theta analogy is lag-locked rather than global-phase; (6) T16 does not test Treves-Rolls. The highest-priority experiments are a time-aligned comparator (E1), a trisynaptic/monosynaptic double dissociation (E2), and a frequency-domain waterbed test of the feedback (E3). Feedback-Transformer and value-residual baselines (E7) are needed before claiming any hippocampal advantage. All repo results cited are small-scale and mostly single-seed.

corrections: docs/design/temporal-loop.md says 'CA1 pyramidal cells do not project back to CA3': viral tracing shows excitatory ventral CA1 -> dorsal CA3 projections, also reaching CA3 interneurons (Lin et al. 2021, 10.1371/journal.pbio.3001127; Lin et al. 2023, 10.1002/cne.25510). The back-projection is mixed-sign, so the op-amp is an abstraction, not anatomy.

Design note claims the loop kernel 'is a sum of damped complex exponentials': the rectified cosine [cos]_+ with a hard onset at Delta>=tau is not a finite sum. It is exactly rho-periodic (w(Delta+tau)=rho w(Delta)), so a factorised-relevance loop admits an exact comb-filter recurrence with a tau-length buffer.

Subtractive feedback is described as a high-pass filter that cuts echo while new content passes. By Bode's sensitivity integral, mean log|S| over frequency = 0 (computed). At K=1 (tau=16, rho=0.9) DC echo is 0.50x, but content at a ~46-token period is amplified 2.51x, and ~48% of frequencies are amplified. T6 tested DC only.

Theta justification of the osc kernel is inaccurate: Hasselmo et al. 2002 use a global phase for encoding/retrieval, but the kernel's phase depends on lag t-s; theta sequences are forward compressed sweeps, not decaying re-expression of past content.

TimeChannel is described as Shankar & Howard's 'time cells': it implements only the Laplace (leaky-integrator) stage, which matches LEC temporal-context cells (Tsao 2018; Bright 2020); hippocampal time cells need the inverse-Laplace stage.

The claim that nothing tells transformers how much time has passed, or 'something LLMs do not currently do', is overstated: RetNet decays, Forgetting Transformer and CoPE supply elapsed-time/salience-count signals.
HippocampalBlock has no EC-II -> CA3 direct input; CA3 queries come only from the DG code, contrary to the Treves & Rolls argument cited elsewhere in the repo.
HippocampalBlock places CA2 (FiLM) serially between CA3 and CA1; anatomically the Schaffer path bypasses CA2, which is a parallel EC-II-driven station (Chevaleyre & Siegelbaum 2010).

CA1 comparator is mistimed: with sequential=True, the query at t retrieves the stored successor (a prediction of t+1) and compares it with x_t. Within-segment values are autoassociative while store values are successors, so one softmax mixes two time indices.

ca1.py docstring conflates conjunction and mismatch: coincident EC-III+CA3 input drives plateaus and plasticity (a conjunction/instructive signal; Takahashi & Magee 2009; Grienberger & Magee 2022). The 'novelty' output is supervised by novelty_alignment_loss on token loss, so it is a distilled surprise predictor, not an intrinsic comparator readout.
The CA1 fusion vector [a;r;a*r;|a-r|] is the NLI heuristic-matching feature (Mou et al. 2015; Conneau et al. 2017) and should be credited.

The 'CA1 -> CA3' subtractive feedback in HippocampalLoop acts at the injection summing junction and never touches CA3 keys, values or relevance; in the default open loop there is no path through CA3 at all.

T16 ('Not supported') does not test Treves-Rolls: read=direct vs read=dg also switches untied W_q vs tied W_k, uses a feedforward lookup rather than attractor completion, and uses a learned (not random) DG code.

Genesis/design claim that the closed regulated timed loop is a 'new organisation': the closed loop of lagged self-states is the Feedback Transformer (Fan 2020); novelty is limited to regulation and timing.

Sik et al. 1994 is anatomical; 'negative-feedback gain control' (REFERENCES.md) is the repo's interpretation.

ca2.summary: The CA2 track recombines published parts; it is not a new mechanism. Biologically, 'societal norms drive CA2' is indefensible. CA2 supports social identity/novelty memory (Hitti & Siegelbaum 2014; Meira 2018; Donegan 2020), is modulated by vasopressin/oxytocin, promotes aggression via lateral septum (Leroy 2018), drifts over hours–days (Mankin 2015), and gates rather than simply boosts ripples (Oliva 2016 vs Kay 2016, Alexander 2018). ca2.py's 'no mossy-fibre input' claim is outdated (Kohara 2014). In ML, every element of the graded escalating controller is published: probe gates (CAST, SafeSwitch, AdaSteer, StTP/StMP), per-step intensity (DAC), PID framing (Nguyen 2025; across layers), token-level cumulative harm (streaming monitor) and multi-turn risk accumulation (THRD). The exact token-level leaky-integral→tanh-gain→refusal-direction hook has no published twin found, so it is partially novel but incremental. As coded it is a soft switch: at λ=0.9, κ=0.5 the gain reaches 0.875·cap after 3 tokens (0.938 after 4) and has a ~10-token time constant, so the multi-turn escalation (A3/H4) cannot occur. The 'loop' closes only through sampled tokens, so the op-amp stability analysis does not transfer. Gist momentum (fast-minus-slow EMA of the model's own residual stream) is the most original idea found; only cross-layer momentum in vision-language(-action) models (STAR, DAMO) and static mean-centring precede it. However, it is open-loop positive feedback, and 'under negative feedback' is unimplemented. SOPHIA's self-loop finding, manifold-steering plateaus and massive activations are concrete risks. A6 is partly anticipated (Arditi 2024; Herbster 2026). Joad 2026 implies selectivity comes from the gate, so A1/J1 and a matched-norm E2 are the decisive first experiments. The notebook's STU-PID citation is withdrawn and its numbers are stale.

corrections: limbic_llm/ca2.py docstring: 'CA2 lacks mossy-fibre input' is outdated; DG granule cells project to CA2 (Kohara et al. 2014, doi:10.1038/nn.3614).
ca2.py docstring: supramammillary input is not unique to CA2 among hippocampal targets; SuM also targets DG with a contextual-novelty signal (Chen et al. 2020).
ca2.py presents Howard–Kahana temporal context as a CA2 property; CA2 drift is on hours–days (Mankin 2015) while ρ=0.9 gives ~10-token memory; temporal context is also documented in LEC (Tsao 2018).
README: serial 'EC → DG → CA3 → CA2 → CA1' misdescribes CA2, which is a parallel route with strong direct EC II input to CA2 and CA2→CA1 output (Chevaleyre & Siegelbaum 2010).
NOTEBOOK alignment proposal: 'social context and norms shape CA2' is unsupported; CA2 encodes social identity/novelty and can promote aggression.
NOTEBOOK/A6: formula h ← h − G·tanh(κE)‖h‖d̂ with d̂ = refusal direction has the wrong sign (would ablate refusal); steering.py correctly adds +g‖h‖d̂.

NOTEBOOK cites 'STU-PID' (arXiv 2506.18831) with GSM8K 81→87%, −32% tokens; the paper is withdrawn by its author in favour of arXiv 2510.04309, and the current version reports 85.7→89.6% and 1026→790 tokens.
NOTEBOOK describes PID Steering as steering strength regulated over generation; its integral term accumulates across layers, not tokens.

steering.py defaults (λ=0.9, κ=0.5): gain reaches 0.46/0.74/0.875/0.938 of the cap after 1–4 tokens (0.967 after 5) of s≈1, time constant ≈10 tokens, and reset() between sequences means A3/H4 multi-turn escalation cannot occur; it needs λ≈0.998 or a turn-level integrator.

steering.py 'open loop' and K2–K3 stability transfer: the probe reads the pre-injection stream at the same layer, so the loop closes only through sampled tokens; the op-amp/characteristic-polynomial analysis does not apply to A4. The leaky integrator has no setpoint, so it is a low-pass gain schedule, not integral control.
probe.py/steering.py: probe trained on last prompt token but applied to every generated token (distribution shift); token-level probes as in streaming-monitor work are needed.
Gist direction does not handle massive activations at delimiter/first tokens (Sun et al. 2024), a predicted confound for the EMA difference.
'Gist momentum under negative feedback' is not implemented: the gist arm is open-loop positive feedback with a cap (R3 planned only).

dg_moe.summary: limbic-llm's DentateGyrus (learned expansion + k-WTA + per-unit gain + reserve units with age-boosted plasticity) is a top-k sparse FFN; as GDN write keys it is a Kanerva-style sparse-address memory. Both are published (k-sparse AE, Ahmad 2019, SDM-MLP Bricken 2023; Kanerva SDM incl. successor sequence storage; Schlag 2021 key expansion; Sparse State Expansion 2025; Mixture-of-Memories 2025). 'DG as MoE gate' holds formally only in the fine-grained limit (PKM/PEER: single-neuron experts selected by top-k), and HiCL already implements a DG-gated MoE. It is functionally wrong for Qwen3/Qwen3-Next/Qwen3.5 coarse routers (128/8, 512/10+1, 256/8+1 provisional), which are trained with load balancing to send similar tokens to the same experts and collapse representations toward centroids: clustering, closer to completion than separation. Repo evidence for a DG benefit is weak: M7 is a ceiling effect, T13 is single seed, and T16 does not test Treves-Rolls because there is no CA3 recurrent completion stage. Biology fixes: mossy cells are excitatory, not inhibitory; mossy-fibre detonation is frequency-dependent, not a static gain; 2007-era DG remapping may reflect mossy cells; immature granule cells are hyperexcitable integrators; human adult neurogenesis is contested. Highest-value experiments: (1) overlap-controlled sparse-vs-dense key capacity above d_k (exact delta-rule capacity is bounded by d_k regardless of sparsity); (2) measure whether Qwen MoE router codes separate or cluster near-duplicates, then use them as side-memory keys vs FlyHash; (3) expert neurogenesis for continual fine-tuning vs ESFT and LoRA, which links to the author's subnetwork-restricted fine-tuning project via ESFT and sparse memory finetuning.

corrections: dentate_gyrus.py docstring: 'Strong feedback inhibition (basket / mossy cells)': mossy cells are excitatory glutamatergic hilar neurons (Scharfman 2016, 10.1038/nrn.2016.87); inhibition is from basket and other GABAergic interneurons.

'Mossy-fibre gain g' as a static learned per-unit scale misrepresents conditional, frequency-dependent detonation (Henze 2002; Vyleta 2016); a faithful analogue gates write strength by recent DG activity.

REFERENCES.md annotates Shazeer 2017 as 'DG as an expert gate', and genesis.md frames 'DG -> MoE gate'. NOTEBOOK R1 already concedes that nothing reuses an MoE router and that routers optimise load balance; coarse routers cluster (Chi 2022; Qiu 2025). The framing should be corrected or restricted to the fine-grained (PEER/PKM) limit and credited to HiCL.

T16 is labelled 'Not supported' for Treves-Rolls, but the temporal loop has no CA3 recurrent completion stage, which the hypothesis requires; the test compares a thresholded vs an unthresholded read. Relabel as not a test of the hypothesis.
M7 'DG faster early' rests on one seed at ceiling (RESULTS §3 acknowledges the task does not separate arms); it should not be read as a DG benefit.

DG separation is asserted from a single cosine in a unit test (pattern_separation); with backprop-trained expansion weights codes may align rather than separate. Measure input-vs-output overlap curves on trained models.
Neurogenesis citation relies only on Spalding 2013; human adult neurogenesis is contested (Sorrells 2018 vs Moreno-Jimenez 2019).

grow() initialises newborn units at Kaiming scale under the same global k-WTA as trained units; whether they are ever recruited is unmonitored (code-review observation, not run). Immature granule cells are hyperexcitable integrators (Aimone 2011).

gdn.summary: The GDN formalism in limbic-llm is published. 'GDN update = one SGD step on the Titans loss at the decayed state' is in the GDN paper itself, Longhorn, Miras and test-time regression (Wang, Shi & Fox 2025). 'One-hot keys = exact RAM' is Kohonen's correlation-matrix memory plus the Schlag et al. 2021 d_k capacity bound. Successor-bound keys are Sompolinsky-Kanter sequence memory, the induction-head and H3-shift mechanism, and the design principle of Memory Mosaics. 'GDN state = CA3' relabels the fast-weight-as-hippocampus view and is biologically weak: CA3 is an autoassociative attractor with Hebbian plasticity, while GDN is a linear heteroassociative, error-corrective readout. Under a linear readout, DG sparsity cannot raise the d_k bound, and the repo's own data agree (tied_x8 = dg_x8 = 1.00). M4 is contradicted by its own numbers: gdn_x8 with d_k=128 fails at 8-32 pairs, so the failure is optimisation, not capacity. M5 never loads the memory beyond d_k. M6 compares against a simplified chunked Titans, and full attention scores only 0.49 on the same task. P1 is expected: HLA (2026) shows needle attenuation in pretrained Qwen3.5 GDN, and G&A, SWAX and hybrid-ratio studies find retrieval concentrated in a few attention heads. P2, where a 4.38M residual module at block 12 recruits frozen GDN layers for exact 500-token recall, is the one partially novel result. It is mechanistically unexplained: the loop kernel is zero at the gap and the loop gain barely moved, so the module behaves as an adapter. It needs parameter-matched adapter, LoRA and state-offset controls plus state probes. W1 is anticipated by δ-mem (2026, a delta-rule state on a frozen Qwen3-4B), and W3 by a crowded replay and LLM-sleep literature (Lee et al. 2026; Behrouz et al. 2026; sparse memory finetuning). Next: E1 (state probing), E2 (adapter controls) and E3 (state-space injection).

novelty.idea: One-hot keys with alpha=beta=1 make the GDN state exact RAM
novelty.rationale: Kohonen 1972 correlation-matrix memory and the Schlag et al. 2021 d_k capacity bound; the repo credits only a blog (Qwenputer). Note alpha, beta are strictly <1 under the code's parametrisation.

novelty.rationale: Fast-weight/attention-as-hippocampus mappings exist (Whittington 2022; Tyulmankov 2021; Gershman 2025); CA3's attractor, Hebbian character fits the linear error-corrective GDN read poorly.

novelty.rationale: The principle is Sompolinsky-Kanter / induction heads / H3 shift / Memory Mosaics; sharing one projection as query and successor write key inside a GDN mixer is a clean simplification but not a new mechanism.

proposed_experiments.title: E1 Probe GDN state for the needle in frozen Qwen3.5
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: With attention windowed, needle digits remain linearly recoverable from some GDN layers' state at the query (P1 is a read failure, not a write failure).
proposed_experiments.design: No side channels. Record per-head S_t for each GDN layer at the answer position; per-layer ridge probe and learned-query probe (decode S q*); HLA-style attenuation ||S(with needle)-S(needle swapped)||/||S|| vs gap. Controls: gap 32, shuffled needle, Qwen3 residual stream.
proposed_experiments.metric: Probe digit accuracy by layer (chance 0.1); attenuation slope vs gap.

proposed_experiments.title: E2 Parameter-matched adapter controls for P2
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Any trainable 4.4M perturbation upstream of GDN layers 13-21 reaches exact recall, so P2 is adaptation rather than hippocampal-loop memory.
proposed_experiments.design: Qwen3.5-2B, attention windowed, gap ~501, 3000 steps, 3 seeds. Arms: current side channels; zero-init residual MLP at block 12 with memory and time off; LoRA on GDN q/k/v/alpha/beta of layers 13-21; state-offset tuning; side channels with loop read zeroed at eval.
proposed_experiments.metric: Exact match, token acc, per-digit CE (C1a), held-out perplexity drift.

proposed_experiments.title: E3 State-space injection instead of residual injection
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Writing side-memory content directly into a downstream GDN state, in that layer's key space, gives recall with fewer params and less perplexity damage than residual injection, including with all layers windowed.
proposed_experiments.design: Side memory (W1 successor GDN or horizon loop) emits (k,v); inject S <- S + gamma v k^T into GDN layers after the tap with k = norm(W_k^(l) x); gamma gated by CA1 novelty. Baselines: residual injection, learned state offset, delta-mem low-rank attention correction. Run S1 saturation sweep first.
proposed_experiments.metric: Needle exact at gaps 500/2k/8k (allwin); WikiText perplexity change; injected-state norm ratio.

proposed_experiments.title: E4 W1 as a head-to-head against delta-mem and same-position keys
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Address shift lifts P4a from one recovered digit to four.
proposed_experiments.design: Qwen3-1.7B allwin; fixed-size side GDN memory d_k in {64,256}; addressing arms: same-position, tied successor, learned short-conv shift; plus delta-mem reproduction; pairs sweep up to 2*d_k.
proposed_experiments.metric: Per-digit CE against the k-digits-known ladder (1.842/1.382/0.921), exact match, recall vs pairs.

proposed_experiments.title: E5 Capacity sweep that can falsify 'exact RAM'
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Linear readout is exact up to P ~ d_k then degrades smoothly; DG sparsity does not move the boundary; softmax/thresholded readout does.
proposed_experiments.design: Pure-GDN small LMs on AssociativeRecall, P in {8..512}, n_keys in {64,1024}, d_k in {16,64,128}; arms gdn (prev-token conv init), tied, dg, DeltaProduct n_h=2, modern-Hopfield readout, tuned softmax attention; LR sweep and 3 seeds.
proposed_experiments.metric: Recall vs P/d_k curves.

proposed_experiments.title: E6 Fair Titans comparison
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: The 1.00 vs 0.48 gap of M6 shrinks with a per-token Titans update and a properly trained attention baseline.
proposed_experiments.design: Per-token Titans (chunk=1, no averaged eta/alpha, no boundary drop) or reference implementation; matched state; retune full attention until it solves 6 pairs; 3 seeds.
proposed_experiments.metric: Recall and learning curves.

proposed_experiments.title: E7 Causal tracing of the needle route in the hybrid
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: With full attention, the needle is carried by a few attention heads (G&A) reading GDN-prepared representations; windowing only those heads reproduces P1.
proposed_experiments.design: Activation and state patching clean vs corrupted needle across GDN and attention layers; identify G&A heads; window only them.
proposed_experiments.metric: Patching recovery fraction per layer and head; exact match when only G&A heads are windowed.

proposed_experiments.title: E8 Consolidating GDN state into weights for never-ending chat
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Distilling segment content into LoRA at boundaries ('sleep') preserves recall of evicted facts better than state alone, and error-prioritised replay beats uniform.
proposed_experiments.design: Qwen3.5-2B on a segment stream with facts queried K segments later. Arms: state only; sleep-LoRA uniform; novelty priority; GDN self-recall-error priority; offline recurrence into state (Lee 2026); SDFT.
proposed_experiments.metric: Fact recall vs K; backward transfer; perplexity and MMLU subset.

proposed_experiments.title: E9 Three-tier memory for KV trimming
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Window KV + sparse exact cache admitted by GDN self-recall error + GDN state beats KV-only eviction at equal cache bytes.
proposed_experiments.design: LoLA-style split on Qwen3.5 using gated_delta_scan's err; baselines SnapKV, H2O, StreamingLLM.
proposed_experiments.metric: RULER needle accuracy at 32k-128k vs cache bytes.

proposed_experiments.title: E10 Multi-hop successor retrieval as pathfinding
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Iterated reads of a tied-address GDN memory solve multi-hop chains a single read cannot; beta in (0,2) adds state tracking.
proposed_experiments.design: Synthetic graph-walk task; iterate read v_{t+1} as next query; side arm with negative eigenvalues.
proposed_experiments.metric: Accuracy vs hop count; parity accuracy.

corrections: M4 ('standard GDN loses recall once stored pairs exceed its key size') is contradicted by results/gdn_capacity.json: gdn (d_k=16) is already 0.426 at 8 pairs (<d_k), and gdn_x8 (d_k=128) is 0.428/0.320/0.222 at 8/16/32 pairs, far below d_k. Failure is not capacity-bound; likely optimisation (single seed, 1500 steps, one LR 3e-3, conv initialised to the current token rather than a shift).

M5 ('exact RAM up to 32 pairs') never loads the memory beyond d_k=128 (64 key tokens); 1.00 is the expected linear-memory result, and the fair comparison is gdn_x8 vs tied_x8 (gdn at d_k=16 has a 8x smaller state). The overwrite ('100% new / 0% old') is the delta rule's defining property (Schlag et al. 2021).

DG sparsity shows no effect: tied_x8 and dg_x8 both 1.00 at every load; under GDN's linear readout sparsity cannot raise the d_k exact-capacity bound (Tsodyks-Feigel'man, Willshaw need non-linear readout). Claims that DG addressing raises GDN capacity should be withdrawn or restated.

M6 compares against a simplified chunked Titans (gradients at chunk start, eta/alpha averaged per chunk, trust-region clip, boundary transition dropped; docstring notes same-key writes add within a chunk), and full attention scores only 0.49 on the same task, so the task/budget does not discriminate. State as 'per-token delta rule beats this Titans re-implementation'.

P2's stated route ('through the GDN layers above the tap') is unsupported as a loop mechanism: the default osc kernel weight is exactly 0 at the ~501 gap, the loop gain moved only 0.2689 -> 0.2697, and TimeChannel integrates a scalar salience (no content). The 4.38M side module acts as an adapter; a parameter-matched adapter control is missing.

gated_delta.py docstring: 'with one-hot keys and alpha = beta = 1 the state is exact RAM' is unreachable under the parametrisation alpha = exp(-softplus(.)) < 1 and beta = sigmoid(.) < 1; with init bias -5, alpha ~ 0.9933 so an association keeps ~3.5% of its strength after 500 tokens unless alpha is learned toward 1.
beta = sigmoid(.) in (0,1) means GDN memories here cannot track parity-like state (Grazzi et al. 2024); relevant if the 'Qwenputer'/RAM framing is extended to computation.

The 'GDN update = one SGD step on the Titans loss' and 'one-hot keys = exact RAM' identities should cite Yang et al. 2024/Longhorn/Miras/Wang-Shi-Fox 2025 and Kohonen 1972/Schlag 2021 rather than only the Qwenputer blog.

W1 should cite and benchmark against delta-mem (Lei et al. 2026, arXiv:2605.12357), which already attaches a delta-rule state to a frozen Qwen3 backbone; W3 needs O-LoRA, sparse memory finetuning, SDFT and uniform-replay baselines.

Biological mapping: GDN's linear, error-corrective, heteroassociative read is not CA3 pattern completion (attractor, Hebbian); one-shot instructive plasticity (BTSP) is documented in CA1; alpha is global down-scaling, not input-specific LTD; 'dg' mode using DG codes for reads contradicts Treves & Rolls' perforant-path retrieval argument (consistent with the repo's own T16).

bib_audit.summary: All 82 entries in docs/references.bib (same key set as REFERENCES.md) exist; none is fabricated. 54 are bibliographically correct, 22 need correction, 5 are misdescribed and 1 (O'Keefe & Nadel 1978) is not machine-verifiable. Systemic issues: no DOIs (49 added, all resolve, none retracted); stale arXiv-only venues (Titans is NeurIPS 2025, HiCL AAAI 2026, Larimar ICML 2024, CAST ICLR 2025, Coconut and SEAL COLM 2025, ASC Findings ACL 2026 with an added author, STIR EMNLP 2026 under a new title, PID steering ICLR 2026); 'Surname and others' author lists for ten reasoning-steering entries; two arXiv retitlings (Turner, Omidi). Web resources: Qwenputer is real (Divyansh Agrawal, Oct 2026, non-peer-reviewed); LAYA is real (Nandakishor Mukkunnoth); Jev is cited via a third-party site, and its method (RLCD) is unpublished. Content misstatements: the GDN-as-one-gradient-step identity that genesis.md presents as derived here is published in the GDN, DeltaNet and Titans papers. TimeChannel implements only the Laplace layer of Shankar & Howard, not time cells. The gain-control reading of Sik 1994 is the project's analogy. Zhao 2025 is over-generalised. Hippoformer is TEM-based spatial memory, not Titans-style. TCM is not a CA2 theory. The 'graded runtime controller' novelty claim is largely anticipated by AdaSteer and PID steering; only the leaky temporal integral is distinct. HiCL anticipates most of the DG-gated MoE track. The corrected bib keeps all keys and adds six verified sources.

pathfinding.summary: Samsonovich & Ascoli (2005, doi:10.1101/lm.85205, verified) model hippocampal retrieval as greedy search through a graph of remembered contexts: CA3->CA3 synapses (J) store traversed transitions; CA3->CA1 synapses (W) store a goal field written at sharp waves by W_ij=max(W_ij,1/(t-t_j)), i.e. hindsight goal relabelling of a shortest-observed-distance table; theta sweeps probe candidate successors and PFC picks the one exciting the goal CA1 unit. At N=10^4 contexts paths are 6.75 vs 4.22 optimal; a re-implementation here reproduces 6.69+/-3.29 vs 4.24+/-0.66 and shows that removing the two-hop CA3 packet tail lengthens paths 4x (single graph/seed, provisional). Its lineage (Muller 1996 cognitive graph, Samsonovich & McNaughton 1997, Teyler & DiScenna index theory) and descendants (SR, reverse/planning replay, Mattar & Daw, CSCG, TEM, Vector-HaSH, endotaxis, DNC, SoRB, HER) mostly do not cite it (OpenAlex: 128 citers). Theta-cycle alternation of futures (Kay 2020) supports its theta prediction; barrier data (Duvelle 2021, Widloski & Foster 2022) place path information in replay rather than place-field gradients. limbic-llm's successor-bound CA3/GDN store is the J matrix and is anticipated (Levy 1996, Jensen & Lisman 1996, DNC temporal links, induction heads, GDN's own token-shift conv); exact-RAM with one-hot keys is anticipated; novelty replay+sleep is anticipated (CLS; Lee et al. 2026 LLM sleep into SSM fast weights is the closest new prior art). The repo lacks the goal field and any multi-hop task; CA3 n_iter does not chain successors. The frozen-Qwen3.5 side-channel recall through downstream GDN layers (P2) is the most original result. Biological issues: CA2 wired in series (Kohara 2014: DG->CA2->CA1deep parallel path; docstring 'CA2 lacks mossy-fibre input' is wrong); store holds content not pointers; SWR mapped only to cortical consolidation. Top experiments: missing-key k-hop recall with chained reads, and a hindsight goal-field path search benchmarked against the S&A reference.

proposed_experiments.title: Missing-key multi-hop recall beyond the window
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Single-read memories solve only k=1; k chained reads through successor-bound memory give ~p^k accuracy; attention degrades with k.
proposed_experiments.design: Chains key->bridge_1->...->value outside a 16-token window, bridges never adjacent to the query; k=1..6. Arms: full/windowed attention, Titans, GDN tied/dg single read, GDN with q_{i+1}=address(o_i) chained reads, CA3 with n_iter fixed to chain. Qwen3.5 variant: needles A->B, B->C at 500/1000 tokens, 1 vs 2 reads of W1 side memory.
proposed_experiments.metric: Exact match vs k; per-hop accuracy; counterfactual bridge-swap following rate.

proposed_experiments.title: Hindsight goal-field path search (S&A W matrix in a GDN)
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: A second delta-rule matrix written at hindsight sharp-wave events turns successor memory into a pathfinder approaching S&A's ~1.6x optimality.
proposed_experiments.design: Random graphs N=1e2..1e4, out-degree 10, presented as random-walk token streams; write address(j)->goal code with gamma^(t-t_j) at random events; test greedy step over enumerated successors scored by goal readout + 0.2 x successor readout. Baselines: BFS, numpy S&A reference (6.69 vs 4.24 at N=1e4), transformer trained on paths, SR field.
proposed_experiments.metric: Success rate, path length / shortest, invalid-edge and loop rates, noise robustness.

proposed_experiments.title: Replay content and direction
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Reverse goal-anchored replay builds goal fields with fewer steps than forward novelty replay; gain x need beats novelty.
proposed_experiments.design: Uniform vs novelty vs reverse-from-salient vs gain x need (need = SR occupancy) priorities under fixed sleep budget.
proposed_experiments.metric: Backward transfer; goal-field path-search success after sleep.

proposed_experiments.title: Barrier reconfiguration
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: S&A max-rule cannot unlearn closed shortcuts; decaying delta-rule or SR fields can, at a reach cost (cf. T5).
proposed_experiments.design: Train on graph, delete edges, compare max-rule, delta-rule (alpha<1), SR goal fields.
proposed_experiments.metric: Invalid-path rate; relearning time; reach.

proposed_experiments.title: Alternating candidates in the temporal loop
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Alternating top-k retrieved candidates across loop periods with CA1 goal selection improves accuracy per reasoning token over gist steering.
proposed_experiments.design: Theta-like alternation of candidate injections during CoT on graph-planning (CogEval-style) then GSM8K; run after S1 gain sweep.
proposed_experiments.metric: Accuracy vs tokens; loop/invalid-step rates; stability.

proposed_experiments.title: Cluster disconnection
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Deleting one bridge binding makes a downstream cluster unreachable; one direct cue restores it (S&A prediction 2).
proposed_experiments.design: Delete bridge in multi-hop task; probe reachability before/after one direct cue.
proposed_experiments.metric: Fraction of downstream nodes reachable.

corrections: limbic_llm/ca2.py docstring says CA2 'lacks mossy-fibre input'; Kohara et al. 2014 (doi:10.1038/nn.3614) showed functional monosynaptic DG->CA2 input.

hippocampal_block.py wires CA2 (FiLM) in series between CA3 and CA1 so all retrieved CA3 content passes through CA2; anatomically CA3->CA1 Schaffer collaterals bypass CA2, and CA2 forms a parallel DG->CA2->CA1-deep circuit (Kohara 2014).

ca3.py describes n_iter as recurrent settling/attractor dynamics, but the query is re-anchored to the cue (xi = h + retrieved); with sequential=True extra iterations retrieve the successor of a cue+successor mixture rather than chaining successors or converging.

replay.py frames sharp-wave replay solely as cortical consolidation and replays whole sequences forward; omits hippocampal-side writing/stabilisation (S&A 2005; Roux 2017; Yang 2024), reverse replay and replay-as-planning (Foster & Wilson 2006; Pfeiffer & Foster 2013).

The CA3 episodic store holds residual-stream content vectors, functionally a selective KV cache; it should not be described as hippocampal indexing (index theory and S&A store pointers, content in neocortex).

code_review.summary: The code is mostly faithful: the Gated DeltaNet scan and chunkwise solver match a literal transcription of the gated delta rule to 1e-15 (fp64), the op-amp ringing threshold reproduces exactly (K=1.680, period 44.1 tokens), and pytest gives 101 passed, 2 skipped (transformers absent). The Titans module is a chunk-level variant (eta/alpha averaged and applied once per chunk, extra update-norm clip, no q/k/v convs), so Titans numbers describe this variant. The headline results need restating. The CPU associative-recall task is teacher-forced with values drawn from 16, so remembering the set of studied values and eliminating revealed ones scores 0.476 with no binding; Strategy I (0.414) is below that ceiling and full attention (0.485) and Titans (0.483-0.490) exceed it by only 0.007-0.014 (<=1.6 binomial SE over 3,072 scored queries), so M1 shows set memory, not binding. The same baseline (0.424/0.319/0.243 at 8/16/32 pairs) matches gdn_x8 (0.428/0.320/0.222), so M4 is not a capacity curve. Only successor-tied GDN memories bind; this is the H3 shift/induction-head mechanism, and M6 is confounded by tied q/k projections. On Qwen3.5 the windowed baseline is below the answer-format floor (loss 4.03), the loop's kernel is zero at the needle lag, and its gain barely moved, so the 1.00 recall is most simply read as adapter repair of a windowing shift, not loop memory; P1 is unsupported until a memory-off adapter control is run. The needle task (one digit string in digit-free filler) is passkey retrieval, not binding. Most components are anticipated (delta rule as test-time regression, k-WTA/DG-gated MoE, FiLM, ActAdd/CAST/PID steering, CLS replay, neurogenesis units). Plausibly new: the regulated re-injection loop analysis (self-rehearsal primacy, delay-limited subtractive feedback) and the graded/gist controllers, which are unrun. The minimal publishable set is Zoology-style MQAR with a binding-free baseline, adapter controls plus RULER on Qwen, multi-seed temporal-loop runs, and standard-protocol alignment arms.

novelty.idea: GDN update equals one SGD step on the Titans associative loss at the decayed state
novelty.rationale: Delta rule as online regression is in Schlag 2021, Yang 2024, TTT (Sun 2024), test-time regression (Wang 2025) and Miras (Behrouz 2025).

novelty.idea: Successor-bound (previous-token) addressing turning GDN state into exact RAM
novelty.rationale: Equivalent to H3's shift-then-bind and the previous-token/induction-head circuit; short convs and Canon layers supply the same shift; Qwenputer blog (repo bib) already states the RAM view. Repo result M5 is a confirmation.

novelty.idea: DG expansion + k-WTA as pattern-separated addresses / MoE gate
novelty.rationale: k-WTA layers (Ahmad 2019), product keys (Lample 2019), PEER (He 2024), SDM continual learner (Bricken 2023), DG-gated MoE (HiCL 2025).

novelty.idea: CA3 novelty-gated episodic slot store with Hopfield retrieval
novelty.rationale: Modern Hopfield = attention (Ramsauer 2020); kNN activation memories (Wu 2022), surprise-gated episodic memory (EM-LLM, Larimar in repo bib).

novelty.idea: CA1 comparator [a;r;a*r;|a-r|] producing novelty
novelty.rationale: Identical to InferSent matching features (Conneau 2017); surprise-as-loss targets are standard in Titans/EM-LLM.

novelty.idea: CA2 FiLM side channel and activation addition as CA2
novelty.rationale: FiLM (Perez 2018), ActAdd/CAA (repo bib); hippocampal labelling is a re-description.

novelty.idea: Graded escalating controller: leaky integral of a harm-probe score drives a capped steering gain
novelty.rationale: Neighbours: CAST (conditional), PID steering (Nguyen 2025), dynamic activation composition (Scalena 2024), adaptive steering (Wang 2024). The multi-turn escalation integral is not published in this form, but no experiment has been run.

novelty.idea: Re-aligning abliterated models with a refusal direction transplanted from the aligned sibling
novelty.rationale: Adding the refusal direction induces refusal (Arditi 2024) and harmfulness is encoded separately from refusal (Zhao 2025, repo bib); cross-model transplant into abliterated weights is a modest extension; unrun; Tan 2024 predicts input-dependent reliability.

novelty.idea: Gist (fast-minus-slow EMA of residual) momentum steering to shorten chain-of-thought
novelty.rationale: Not found in this form; nearest are concise-CoT vectors (Azizi 2025), SEAL, manifold steering. Not wired into run.py and not run.

novelty.idea: Temporal loop: lagged content-addressed re-injection with clamped damped-sinusoid kernel
novelty.rationale: Functionally one extra full-range attention head with an age kernel (ALiBi/FoX family) plus feedback (Feedback Transformer, TransformerFAM). The kernel shape and the regulated injection are new, but O(T) memory and phase nulls are drawbacks.

novelty.idea: Control-theoretic analysis of re-injection (divisive vs subtractive, delay-limited critical gain, self-rehearsal primacy in closed loops)
novelty.rationale: Op-amp and delayed-feedback stability are textbook (verified K_crit=1.680); applying them to activation loops and the primacy-by-rehearsal finding appear new but rest on one seed per arm.

novelty.idea: Time channel: salience-driven log-spaced leaky integrators/oscillators
novelty.rationale: Shankar & Howard Laplace layer (repo bib), real-decay linear RNNs, CoPE (Golovneva 2024). The what/when dissociation result is a clean small demonstration.

novelty.idea: Novelty-prioritised replay with sleep updates of slow parameters and logit distillation
novelty.rationale: CLS theory, DER (Buzzega 2020), brain-inspired replay (van de Ven 2020), prioritised replay; no ablation isolating novelty priority.

novelty.idea: DG neurogenesis reserve units with hyper-plastic young units
novelty.rationale: Neurogenesis deep learning (Draelos 2016); boost is neutralised by Adam and grow() is never exercised.

novelty.idea: Side channels at mid-depth of a frozen GDN hybrid restoring needle recall under windowed attention
novelty.rationale: Interesting empirical observation about hybrids, but confounded with adapter repair of a windowing distribution shift; mechanism untested.

novelty.idea: CA3-CA1 / EC-III->CA1 skip connections as architecture improvement
novelty.rationale: Value residuals (Zhou 2024), DenseFormer (Pagliardini 2024), Hyper-connections (Zhu 2024); repo has no experiment for this track.

proposed_experiments.title: E1 Zoology MQAR re-benchmark with binding-free baseline
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Properly trained full attention, standard GDN and deep Titans all bind; tied/DG addresses help only in sample efficiency or near load = d_k.
proposed_experiments.design: Zoology MQAR generator (vocab 8192, len 64-512, 4-64 pairs); widths 64/128/256; full attn, SWA, repo GDN, GDN with random-init conv, GDN tied, GDN dg, Titans deep, Titans-GDN, Strategy I; 4 LRs x 3 seeds; factorial for M6 (tied q/k x linear/deep x per-token/chunk x heads). ~1,100 runs x ~3 min = ~55 GPU-h (<1.5 days on 2x RTX 5090).
proposed_experiments.metric: MQAR accuracy, first-query accuracy (no elimination possible), gap to bag-of-values ceiling; best-LR per width; mean and bootstrap 95% CI over seeds.

proposed_experiments.title: E2 Adapter controls and RULER on frozen Qwen
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: On Qwen3.5 a memory-free adapter of equal size restores needle recall (GDN carried the needle); on Qwen3 only a loop with a covering horizon helps.
proposed_experiments.design: Qwen3.5-2B and Qwen3-1.7B; arms: frozen windowed; trained adapter with loop+clock off (4.38M params); LoRA r=16 on tap block; clock only; default loop; horizon loop; horizon loop + GDN side store with successor keys (W1); 3 seeds; 6,000 steps. Eval RULER S-NIAH-1/2/3, MK-NIAH, MV-NIAH at 1k/2k/4k with UUID values; per-digit logging. 42 runs x ~20 min = ~15 GPU-h.
proposed_experiments.metric: Exact match, per-token accuracy, per-digit CE against format floor; mean +/- CI over seeds.
proposed_experiments.extends: P1, P2, P4, P4a, W1, C1a, g2b, O5

proposed_experiments.title: E3 Chained successor retrieval (pathfinding)
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Iterating successor lookups k times (Samsonovich & Ascoli pathfinding) recovers all digits/tokens of a multi-token value where one-step lookup recovers one.
proposed_experiments.design: GDN side memory with successor keys on all-windowed Qwen models; 1, 2, 4 chained reads per generated token; RULER multi-hop variable tracking. ~5 GPU-h within E2.
proposed_experiments.metric: Exact match; accuracy by value position; multi-hop tracing accuracy.

proposed_experiments.title: E4 Separate memory from domain adaptation in perplexity
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Most of the WikiText perplexity gain is adaptation, not long-range memory.
proposed_experiments.design: Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 windowed; arms frozen, parameter-matched LoRA trained on WikiText, side with memory ablated, default kernel, horizon kernel; 3 seeds; 30 runs x ~7 min (<4 GPU-h). Add BABILong/PG-19 long-range evaluation.
proposed_experiments.metric: Perplexity overall and on tokens whose predictive context lies > W back (e.g. second occurrences of rare n-grams); BABILong accuracy.

proposed_experiments.title: E5 Multi-seed temporal-loop suite
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Stability (T3), subtractive-only learning (T9) and the primacy/recency ordering (T11-T15) survive 5 seeds.
proposed_experiments.design: Rerun the 14 scripted configurations x 5 seeds; replace zero-shot recency probe with a trained recency task with curriculum on separation; ~70 CPU runs x 15 min = ~16 CPU-h (~2 h wall on 16 cores).
proposed_experiments.metric: What/when accuracy, echo ratio by range, newer/older naming; stratified bootstrap 95% CI (Agarwal 2021).

proposed_experiments.title: E6 DG pattern separation under key similarity and overload
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Sparse DG addresses reduce interference only when keys are similar or load exceeds d_k; DG on the write path only (Treves-Rolls) beats DG on both paths for noisy cues.
proposed_experiments.design: MQAR with controlled key cosine rho in {0,0.5,0.8,0.95} and shared-prefix keys; loads P/d_k in {0.5,1,2,4}; arms dense tied, learned DG k-WTA 2/5/10%, fixed random expansion+k-WTA, product keys, top-k experts; write-only vs read+write DG; 5 seeds; ~300 runs, ~25 GPU-h.
proposed_experiments.metric: Recall vs similarity and load; interference index; cue-noise completion curve.

proposed_experiments.title: E7 Replay controls
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Novelty priority and sleep add nothing over uniform replay at equal buffer size on easy tasks; differences appear only with small buffers and overlapping keys.
proposed_experiments.design: 10 sequential fact tasks with overlapping keys; buffers 16/64/256; arms naive, uniform, reservoir, DER++, EWC, novelty-prioritised, sleep-only, awake-only; 5 seeds; CPU, a few hours. Then LoRA consolidation on a frozen model (W3).
proposed_experiments.metric: Average accuracy, backward transfer with CI.

proposed_experiments.title: E8 Alignment arms on standard protocols
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: The graded controller matches static steering's harmful-refusal rate at lower over-refusal and capability cost.
proposed_experiments.design: Qwen3-1.7B aligned/abliterated/base; arms none, static CAA, CAST, PID (Nguyen 2025), graded, graded_self; probe/direction from 3 disjoint splits, probe trained on one distribution and tested on another; full XSTest (450), OR-Bench, HarmBench classifier, StrongREJECT; WildGuard or Llama Guard as second judge; MMLU, GSM8K, perplexity. Selectivity curves over gain, compared at matched over-refusal. <10 GPU-h.
proposed_experiments.metric: Harmful refusal / StrongREJECT score vs over-refusal (curve and AUC); capability deltas; probe AUROC and ECE in/out of distribution; bootstrap CI.

proposed_experiments.title: E9 Gist steering of reasoning
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Gist momentum steering shortens reasoning at equal accuracy better than budget forcing.
proposed_experiments.design: Qwen3 thinking 1.7B and 4B; GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME 2024-25 (8 samples/problem); arms full thinking, no-think, budget forcing at matched budgets, SEAL, concise vector, gist at 3 gains after S1 saturation sweep; ~9M tokens per arm, 1-2 days on 2 GPUs. Wire gist into run.py with static gain (graded mode without probe gives zero gain).
proposed_experiments.metric: Accuracy vs mean reasoning tokens (Pareto front), paired bootstrap; flip and 'wait' rates.

proposed_experiments.title: E10 Skip-connection track at small LM scale
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: A temporoammonic (embedding-to-late-comparator) skip does not beat value residuals, DenseFormer or hyper-connections at matched parameters.
proposed_experiments.design: 125M-param models on 2.5B tokens; 5 arms (baseline, temporoammonic skip, value residual, DenseFormer, hyper-connections); 3 seeds; ~15 runs x 5 h = ~75 GPU-h.
proposed_experiments.metric: Validation perplexity, MQAR, RULER at 4k.

corrections: M1 / RESULTS §1 / README: assoc-recall scores do not show binding. Teacher-forced shuffled queries with values from 16 allow a binding-free bag-of-values + elimination strategy scoring 0.476 (per position 0.288, 0.307, 0.337, 0.395, 0.531, 1.000; simulated, 200k sequences). Strategy I 0.414 is below it; full attention 0.485, titans_mac 0.483 and titans_seq 0.490 exceed it by 0.009, 0.007 and 0.014, i.e. 1.0, 0.7 and 1.5 binomial SE (SE ~0.009 for 3,072 scored queries), so they are statistically indistinguishable from the binding-free ceiling.

RESULTS §1 'Not a task ceiling' argument: the full-attention per-position profile 0.26->0.82 is the elimination signature, and its first-query accuracy (0.26) is below the binding-free first-query value (0.288). 'Titans matches full attention' means both learned the same heuristic.

M4 / README 'Standard Gated DeltaNet loses recall once stored pairs exceed its key dimension (0.43 -> 0.13)': binding-free baseline at 8/16/32 pairs is 0.424/0.319/0.243 and gdn_x8 scores 0.428/0.320/0.222; gdn scores 0.426 at 8 pairs (< d_k=16). Standard GDN never learned binding, so this is not a capacity result.

M6 'exact delta-rule memory beats Titans' deep memory' is confounded: titans_gdn also ties wq = wk in sequential mode (a hard-wired previous-token address), uses 4 memory heads, per-token updates and no trust-region clip, while NeuralMemory keeps separate wq/wk. Needs a factorial ablation.
M2 marked Refuted and M7 Open on a task that only tied addressing solves; neither DG writes nor CA1 novelty-lr could show a benefit there. M2 should be Open.

neural_memory.py is a chunk-level Titans variant: eta and alpha averaged over the chunk and momentum/decay applied once per chunk (Titans keeps them per token within the chunk), plus max_update_norm=4 trust region and max_lr=0.4 not in Titans; q/k/v convolutions absent; MAC output gate o = y * M*(y) omitted. All 'Titans' numbers refer to this variant.

P1 'Qwen3.5's GDN layers alone do not recall a needle 500 tokens back' is unsupported: the windowed baseline (attention windowed, GDN intact) has digit loss 4.03 and token accuracy 0.056, below the 1.84 / 0.28 answer-format floor, i.e. the untrained windowed model is out of distribution. The 1.00 recall with side channels coincides with loop kernel weight exactly 0 at the needle lag and gain 0.2689 -> 0.2697, consistent with adapter repair. A memory-off adapter / LoRA control is required; the layer-22 control does not discriminate.
P2 route hypothesis should be stated as one of two: re-injection through later GDN layers vs adapter repair of the windowing shift with GDN carrying the needle throughout.
Needle task (pairs=1, digit-free filler) contains exactly one digit string: it is passkey retrieval and needs no key-value binding; RULER S-NIAH/MK/MV variants are needed before claims about memory.
P4a 'equals exactly one digit known' is one decomposition consistent with mean loss 1.381 and accuracy 0.461; other per-digit mixtures fit; should be a hypothesis until per-digit logging (C1a).

T11-T14 marked Supported (some 'weakly') on one seed each with a zero-shot out-of-distribution two-event probe; T15 already shows seeds disagreeing (0.54 vs 0.38). Should be Open; the analogy to the psychological primacy effect is a hypothesis.

T6/T7 are analytic properties of the linear delayed loop (independently verified: K_crit = 1.680, period 44.1 tokens for tau=16, rho_E=0.9); '3 untrained seeds' adds no evidence. With the default clamp on, subtractive feedback changes only injection direction, so the op-amp law does not describe the deployed ca1_control configuration.

M3 'prevents forgetting': the 256-sequence buffer holds essentially every fact of every prior task (8 keys/task, ~12 pairs/sequence); no uniform-replay, DER, sleep-only or awake-only arm; novelty priority untested. Status should be 'replay works; priority and sleep untested'.

DG neurogenesis: grow() is never called in any experiment, and the per-unit gradient boost is a gradient rescale that Adam/AdamW normalises away (x5 gradient scaling changed a 50-step AdamW trajectory by 1.2e-7). Neurogenesis claims in docs are untested.

ca3.py docstring: 'iterated n_iter times with tied weights (recurrent settling)' — the update xi = h + W_o(softmax(.) V) is residual attention with untied value/output projections, not the Hopfield update; all experiments use n_iter=1.
ca3.py sequential mode mixes semantics in one softmax: store slots return successors (wv(h_{t+1})) while current-segment keys return their own values (wv(h_t)).

Titans and GatedDeltaMemory DG modes compute the read query through the same DG code as the write key, contrary to the Treves-Rolls split (DG for encoding, perforant path for retrieval) the repo cites; only HippocampalLoop offers read='direct'.

ca2.py: 'CA2 lacks mossy-fibre input' and receives projections 'no other CA field gets' are inaccurate: DG input to CA2 was reported by Kohara et al. 2014 (doi:10.1038/nn.3614); supramammillary fibres also target DG; CA2 is distinguished by strong EC-II drive and output to CA1 (Chevaleyre & Siegelbaum 2010).

TimeChannel is described as Shankar-Howard time cells; it implements only the Laplace-domain leaky integrators (closer to LEC temporal context, Tsao et al. 2018); time cells require the inverse transform.
ca2.py TemporalContext called 'slowly drifting', but init rho=0.9 gives a ~10-token time constant truncated at 64 tokens.

CPU assoc-recall windowed baseline still uses sliding windows: 3 layers x (16-1) = 45-token reach exceeds the 41-token distance from the last study value to the first query; the C2 block-window fix was applied only to pretrained runs (the baseline did not exploit it).

gated_delta.py initialises the short causal convolutions to the identity (fla uses random init), so standard 'gdn' mode starts with no token shift; a plausible cause of standard GDN never learning binding in 1,500 steps. Decay gate uses a single bias (-5) rather than fla/Mamba-2's per-head A and dt_bias spread.

Alignment harness: the gist direction is implemented in steering.py but not wired into run.py; graded mode without a probe silently yields zero gain (b = -30); the probe is fitted on harmful_behaviors vs harmless_alpaca, a stylistic split; refusal is substring-judged; --n-eval 64 gives about +/-12-point 95% CI at p=0.5, too wide for the expected selectivity differences.
